messages:
jamie: Heads up — hit a weird routing/quota edge with embeddings. Sent a mixed-dim batch (one 1536, three 768) and the router split them across two model routes. Tenant got double-charged on the high-dim route and experienced a slower fallback for the rest. :face_with_raised_eyebrow:

sara: Ugh. Are we still routing by total bytes? I thought we had a dim-hint header to prefer same-variant grouping.

thomas: We route primarily by size affinity right now (bytes -> route). There27s a shape-hint header but it27s advisory. For mixed dims the splitter treats items independently which can send them to different model variants.

jamie: Example request (redacted):
```
POST /v1/embeddings
Headers: {"Content-Type": "application/json", "X-Embed-Dims": "[1536,768,768,768]"}
Body: {"input": ["p1","p2","p3","p4"]}
```
Router split p1 -> model-x-1536, p2/3/4 -> model-y-768. Billing/quotas incremented per-route.

aisha: Telemetry note: we currently tag route decisions but not "mixed_dims". Would be useful to identify how often this pattern happens and which tenants hit quota regressions. I can add a tag like `embed.mixed_dims:true` + `embed.max_dim:1536`.

leo: From console/UX POV: we should warn in the preflight and show an estimated per-route cost before confirm. Customers will want to see if a single API call can blow through multiple quota buckets.

sara: Agreed. Two parallel asks: (1) short-term runtime opt-in to prefer "coalesce by max-dim" for same-batch; (2) console preflight warning + estimate.

thomas: Short-term runtime change note: coalescing by max-dim is simple but may increase latency for small-dim items (they'd run on bigger model). We can make it opt-in per-tenant or per-route policy. Also propose a heuristic: if max_dim / min_dim <= 2 => coalesce, else keep splitter to avoid huge cost increase.

jamie: That heuristic sounds reasonable. For this tenant the ratio = 1536/768 = 2 -> would coalesce. Would have prevented the double-charge.

aisha: I'll add telemetry and a dashboard tile: "mixed-dim batches" with percent that coalesced vs split, per-tenant cost delta. Also emit `router.policy=coalesce_max_dim` when applied.

leo: Console UX: add a small badge on embeddings route config: "Coalesce mixed dims (canary)" with a tooltip and link to docs. Also add a per-request preflight modal with cost estimates when enabled.

thomas: Implementation plan:
- PR: router: add policy `coalesce_by_max_dim` behind feature flag, default off. (I can do this.)
- Heuristic param (ratio threshold) as tenant override.
- Emit telemetry tags (aisha) and preflight API hook (sara/console) that queries router for estimated route mapping.

sara: Console side tasks:
- Add preflight call in SDK + UI component to surface estimates.
- Add warn banner when mixed dims detected and coalesce flag is off.
I27ll pair with aisha on telemetry fields so UI can display numbers.

aisha: I'll add metrics: `embed.mixed_batches.count`, `embed.mixed_batches.coalesced.count`, `embed.mixed_batches.cost_delta.p50/p90`. Will tag by tenant and route.

leo: Product question: default on or off for new tenants? My preference: off by default, show console recommendation + one-click enable, and auto-enable for tenants that hit > 5 mixed batches/day and consent.

jamie: For the immediate mitigation for the impacted tenant can we flip the flag?

thomas: I can flip in canary env and push a canary rollout. PR coming today.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment scheduled: router-coalesce-feature -> canary cluster at 2024-11-02T18:30:00Z (job 4521).

jamie: Thanks. After deploy let's validate with a synthetic mixed-dim load and check telemetry for `embed.mixed_batches.coalesced.count` and per-tenant quota deltas.

thomas: Action items assigned: thomas -> PR + flip canary; aisha -> telemetry + dashboard tile; sara -> console preflight UI; leo -> product toggle text + docs. I'll drop the PR link once open.

sara: Also note: billing team wants an audit event when a single API call consumes multiple quota buckets. We should emit `billing.audit.multi_route_usage` with request id.

aisha: adding that to the telemetry plan.

jamie: Great. Keep this thread updated with PR and canary results. :thumbsup:
